abstracts.abstract: Traditional information retrieval models assume static user information needs, yet empirical evidence reveals that user requirements evolve dynamically during search sessions. This paper introduces the Adaptive Information Seeking Paradigm (AISP), a novel theoretical framework that conceptualizes information needs as dynamic, goal-directed processes rather than static query representations. The AISP incorporates three core components: need emergence, knowledge construction, and satisfaction crystallization, which collectively explain the temporal dynamics of user behavior in interactive retrieval environments. We conducted a longitudinal user study with 486 participants across 12,000 search sessions to validate the theoretical constructs. Structural equation modeling results demonstrate that the AISP explains 67% of variance in user satisfaction outcomes, significantly outperforming the Cognitive Model of Information Seeking (ΔR² = 0.23). The framework introduces measurable constructs including need perturbation rate and knowledge gap indices that enable precise prediction of user behavior transitions. This paradigm shift fundamentally reorients information retrieval research from query-document matching to holistic user need modeling. The AISP provides actionable implications for designing adaptive search engines and personalized recommendation systems that can anticipate and respond to evolving user requirements in real-time. This work opens new research directions at the intersection of user modeling, information behavior theory, and adaptive system design.

The Probability Ranking Principle (PRP) has served as the foundational theoretical basis for information retrieval for over four decades. However, the assumption of document independence and static relevance estimation fundamentally limits its applicability in modern search engines where contextual signals and user feedback continuously influence relevance judgments. This paper presents the Contextual Dynamic PRP (CD-PRP), an extended theoretical framework that incorporates query-context interaction and time-varying relevance signals into the ranking optimization process. The CD-PRP introduces a contextual relevance function that modulates document relevance scores based on query intent classification, user historical behavior patterns, and temporal search context. We formalize the expected utility maximization problem under contextual constraints and derive optimal ranking policies that account for position bias and examination probability within the updated framework. Theoretical analysis proves that CD-PRP reduces to the classical PRP when contextual signals are uniformly distributed, establishing backward compatibility. Extensive experiments on TREC benchmarks demonstrate that ranking functions derived from CD-PRP achieve statistically significant improvements over PRP-based baselines, with NDCG@10 improvements ranging from 8.3% to 14.7% across diverse query types. This work significantly extends the theoretical foundations of modern retrieval systems while maintaining mathematical elegance and practical interpretability.

Knowledge-aware recommendation systems have demonstrated superior performance by incorporating external knowledge graphs, yet existing approaches predominantly rely on entity-level modeling that fails to capture complex semantic relationships across different knowledge dimensions. This paper introduces Heterogeneous Knowledge-Enhanced Graph Neural Networks (HK-GNN), a novel recommendation architecture that fundamentally reimagines knowledge graph integration through multi-granular semantic reasoning. HK-GNN operates on a meta-path heterogeneous graph structure comprising users, items, entities, and relationship types, employing a hierarchical attention mechanism that first aggregates intra-relation semantics before cross-relation semantic synthesis. The architecture introduces knowledge-guided user preference propagation that models how entity attributes influence item relevance through learned relationship pathways. We design an efficient mini-batch training algorithm that reduces computational complexity from O(V²) to O(V·K) where K represents average neighborhood size, enabling deployment on large-scale industrial datasets. Extensive offline evaluation on Amazon, Last.fm, and a proprietary e-commerce dataset containing 50 million user interactions demonstrates that HK-GNN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art knowledge-enhanced recommenders by 12.4% in AUC and 18.7% in hit ratio at top-20. Online A/B testing in a major video streaming platform over 30 days confirms substantial improvements in user engagement metrics. This paradigm establishes a new direction for knowledge graph utilization in recommender systems through principled semantic reasoning.

Large-scale search engines face inherent tension between ranking quality and computational efficiency when serving billions of queries daily. Existing multi-stage ranking pipelines suffer from suboptimal stage configuration and rigid feature engineering that fail to adapt to query complexity variations. This paper presents AdaRank, an adaptive multi-stage ranking system that dynamically configures ranking stages based on real-time query difficulty estimation and computational budget constraints. AdaRank introduces a lightweight neural query classifier that predicts query complexity using only query text features, enabling informed cascade decisions without expensive historical click analysis. The system employs learned stage skipping policies that bypass unnecessary ranking stages for simple navigational queries while applying full pipeline depth for complex informational queries. We redesign the feature computation layer with intelligent caching and approximate computation strategies that maintain ranking quality while reducing average feature retrieval latency by 62%. Extensive evaluation on Bing search logs comprising 120 million query-document pairs demonstrates that AdaRank achieves 94.3% of full-pipeline ranking quality while operating at 2.8× throughput improvement. The system has been deployed in production serving over 500 million queries daily, achieving 15% reduction in data center computational load and 8% improvement in user satisfaction metrics. This work significantly advances the state-of-the-art in industrial-scale ranking system optimization.
